scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a paginated and filtered list of user ban records as a moderator or administrator. Validate listing and searching by member, moderator, permanence, timeframes, expiration, and reason. Verify response is paginated and matches the applied filter criteria, including cases of (a) no filters (default list), (b) filter by member with at least one ban, (c) filter by moderator, (d) filter by permanence (permanent vs non-permanent), and (e) filters with no matching results. Confirm only admins and moderators can access this endpoint, and non-privileged access is denied.

dependencies.purpose: Create member(s) to apply bans and act as search filter targets.
Create several bans with varying parameters (moderator, permanence, member, reason, and timeframes) for filter diversity.

scenarios.draft: Test successful retrieval of ban details using a valid ban UUID as a moderator or administrator. Validate all returned fields (member, moderator, reason, status, times). Ensure proper access control: only moderators and administrators can retrieve ban details. Attempt to retrieve as unauthorized user and verify access is denied. Attempt to retrieve a non-existent ban and expect a 404 or not found error result.

dependencies.purpose: Create a ban to retrieve and verify returned details and fields.
Create a member as the target of the ban for test setup.

scenarios.draft: Test successful creation of a new ban record by an administrator or moderator, specifying required fields (member_id, moderator_id, reason, permanent flag) and optional expiry. Check response contains all required ban fields and audit data. Confirm that permanent and temporary (with expires_at) bans are correctly recorded. Validate error handling: (a) creating a ban on a member who already has a permanent ban returns an error, (b) attempting to ban a non-existent member yields a not found error, (c) passing an expires_at in the past for a temporary ban triggers a validation error, and (d) non-privileged users are denied ban creation rights.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member account as the target of the ban.
Create a member to be the moderator/admin who applies the ban.

scenarios.draft: Test updating details of an existing ban by a moderator or admin. (a) Successfully update ban_reason, permanence, and expires_at for a currently active temporary ban, confirming returned record is updated. (b) Attempt to update a non-existent or soft-deleted ban by ID and expect a not found error. (c) Try to set expires_at to a past value and confirm validation error. (d) Attempt to toggle permanent status for an expired or deleted ban and confirm update is rejected or fails per business logic. (e) Try updating the ban with insufficient rights (not as mod/admin) and check for permission error.

dependencies.purpose: Create an active ban record to update.

scenarios.draft: Test deleting (lifting) a ban as a moderator or administrator, using ban ID. (a) Successfully soft-delete an active ban and ensure deleted_at is set, ban is no longer active, but preserved for audit. (b) Attempt to delete a non-existent or already deleted ban; expect not found or suitable error. (c) Attempt to delete a ban as a non-authorized user and confirm operation is denied. (d) Attempt a repeat delete on a ban and confirm correct error is returned. Also, verify that audit logs are updated as per compliance requirements.

dependencies.purpose: Create an active ban record to be deleted/soft-deleted in the test.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a paginated and filtered list of subscriptions for an authenticated user. Provide various filter conditions such as target type (thread, section), partial name matches, date ranges, and page/size settings in the request. Validate that only the user's own (non-deleted) subscriptions are returned, the filters are correctly applied, and the results respect pagination and sorting. Ensure unauthorized users cannot access other users' subscription data. Check that deleted or unsubscribed records are omitted. Validate failure cases for invalid parameters or authorization context.

dependencies.purpose: A member must be registered to perform authenticated subscription searches.
The member should have at least one active subscription to validate list retrieval and filtering.

scenarios.draft: Test successfully retrieving the detail for a specific subscription by its UUID for the authenticated owner. Confirm all metadata is correct and matches the subscription. Ensure that deleted subscriptions return appropriate error responses (not found or gone).

dependencies.purpose: Register a member to own and access the subscription.
Member must have an active subscription to retrieve.

scenarios.draft: Test that attempting to fetch subscription details by a user who does not own the subscription results in a forbidden or not found response, ensuring privacy/security compliance.

dependencies.purpose: Register two separate member accounts to differentiate ownership.
Create a subscription for the first user; the second user will attempt to access it.

scenarios.draft: Test creating a new subscription for the authenticated user to follow a valid content item (e.g., thread, section, or tag). The request should specify a valid target_type and target_id that exist and are eligible for subscription. Upon success, verify the returned object matches input data, and enforce business rules on uniqueness and ownership.

dependencies.purpose: Register an authenticated user to create the subscription.

scenarios.draft: Test error handling when attempting to create a duplicate subscription (same member, target_type, and target_id combination) for a user. The system should return a conflict or duplicate error and prevent the duplicate. This enforces schema uniqueness and prevents redundant notifications.

dependencies.purpose: Register the member.
Establish the initial subscription for the unique member-target pair.

scenarios.draft: Test that providing an invalid, forbidden, or non-existent target_id or target_type (such as banned, deleted, or unsupported type) results in appropriate error responses, such as 404 or 400, and does not create a subscription.

dependencies.purpose: Register the member so they can attempt to create a subscription.

scenarios.draft: Test updating the allowed fields (such as notification or preference settings) of a subscription for the authenticated user. Ensure only permitted fields are updated, changes are persisted, and the response reflects the new subscription state. Also, validate that a user cannot update a subscription they do not own (forbidden).

dependencies.purpose: Register a user to own a subscription.
Create a subscription belonging to the member for update.

scenarios.draft: Test that updating a subscription that is deleted or does not exist results in appropriate error responses, such as not found or gone, and does not modify/create data.

dependencies.purpose: Register a user for the operation.

scenarios.draft: Test successfully deleting (unsubscribing) a subscription by its authenticated owner using the subscription's UUID. Validate that the record is soft-deleted or removed as per business rules, is omitted from future queries, and that audit logging confirms the correct operation. Ensure attempts to delete already-deleted or non-existent subscriptions are gracefully handled with not found/gone responses.

dependencies.purpose: Register the subscription owner.
Create a subscription to be deleted by the owner.

scenarios.draft: Test that attempting to delete another member's subscription fails with a forbidden error. This ensures only subscription owners may perform delete operations and upholds privacy and security requirements.

dependencies.purpose: Register two member accounts: one as owner, one as external user.
Create a subscription for the first member, and have the second user attempt the delete.

scenarios.draft: Test that an administrator can successfully retrieve a paginated list of discussion_board_configurations, using valid filter and pagination parameters. Ensure only configurations the admin has access to are returned. Steps: Authenticate as administrator, call the PATCH endpoint with sample filter and pagination parameters, verify that the response is a paginated object containing matching configuration records. Confirm metadata fields such as created_at and updated_at are present.

dependencies.purpose: Create an administrator member account to obtain admin privileges for subsequent API calls.
Assign administrator privileges to the created member to enable configuration management actions.

scenarios.draft: Test that a non-administrator (e.g., regular member or guest) is forbidden from retrieving the configuration list. Steps: Create a regular member or use unauthenticated/guest context, attempt to call the PATCH endpoint, verify that the system returns a forbidden (HTTP 403) error response and no data is disclosed.

dependencies.purpose: Create a regular member account for attempting access without admin rights.

scenarios.draft: Test that an administrator may retrieve detailed information for a specific configuration by its UUID. First, create an admin, create a configuration record, then call the GET endpoint with the configuration's UUID. Verify the returned data includes the expected key, value, description, and appropriate audit fields (created_at, updated_at).

dependencies.purpose: Create an administrator account to perform configuration operations.
Grant admin privileges to the created user.
Create a configuration record to be retrieved in detail for this test.

scenarios.draft: Test that requesting details for a non-existent configuration UUID returns a not found (404) error. Steps: Authenticate as administrator, call the GET endpoint using a random/unused UUID, verify correct error response and that no sensitive data is returned.

dependencies.purpose: Create an administrator account to use for authorized requests.
Grant admin privileges to the created user.

scenarios.draft: Test creating a new configuration record as an administrator with a unique valid key/value/description. Step sequence: Authenticate as admin, call POST with valid params, verify that the response contains the created configuration with correct metadata and that it is retrievable via list/detail endpoints.

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin member for configuration creation.
Grant administrator rights to the member.

scenarios.draft: Test that creating a configuration with a duplicate key is rejected. Steps: Setup an administrator and create a configuration with a unique key, then attempt to create another configuration with the same key. Verify the system returns a conflict/error indicating key uniqueness violation.

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin member.
Grant administrator role to the member.
Create the initial configuration to occupy the target key.

scenarios.draft: Test successful update of an existing configuration by admin. Steps: Create admin and configuration, then update the configuration's value, key, and/or description with valid data. Confirm updated record is returned with new audit info.

dependencies.purpose: Create an administrator for update test.
Promote member to admin.
Create a configuration to update.

scenarios.draft: Test that updating a configuration's key to one already used by another configuration is rejected. Steps: Create admin and two configuration records with unique keys, then attempt to update the second configuration's key to match the first. Confirm that an error/conflict is returned due to key uniqueness rules.

dependencies.purpose: Create admin member for configuration operations.
Assign administrator privileges.
Create the first configuration with the initial key.
Create the second configuration to be updated.

scenarios.draft: Test updating a non-existent configuration returns not found error. Steps: Authenticate as admin, call PUT using a random/invalid UUID, and verify a not found (404) is returned.

dependencies.purpose: Create admin member.
Promote member to admin.

scenarios.draft: Test successful soft deletion of a configuration by administrator. Steps: Setup admin and create configuration, then call DELETE for its ID. Verify that deleted_at is set and configuration is no longer returned in active lists but retains audit history.

dependencies.purpose: Create administrator member.
Assign admin privileges.
Create a configuration to be deleted.

scenarios.draft: Test soft deletion returns not found error when configuration UUID does not exist. Steps: Authenticate as admin, call DELETE using a random/invalid UUID, verify a not found (404) error occurs.

dependencies.purpose: Create administrator member.
Assign admin privileges.

scenarios.draft: Verify that an authenticated user (member, moderator, or administrator) can retrieve a filtered, paginated list of their notifications. Prepare test users of each allowed role, generate various notification events with differing read/unread statuses, types, and timestamps. Test that the response includes only notifications for the authenticated user and supports different pagination, sorting, and filter options such as unread status and date range.

dependencies.purpose: Register user accounts with different roles to generate data for notification tests.
Seed the system with a set of relevant notification events for the test user.

scenarios.draft: Ensure that if an unauthenticated request is made to list notifications, the endpoint responds with an authorization error and does not reveal notification information.

Test that a member can retrieve a specific notification by its ID, receiving the full details if the notification exists and belongs to them. Prepare a user, trigger a notification, and request its details as that user.

dependencies.purpose: Create a test member account.
Generate a notification for the member to use for retrieval.

scenarios.draft: Verify that a notification cannot be retrieved by a user other than its recipient. Register two users, generate a notification for User A, and attempt to access it as User B, expecting a forbidden or not found response according to privacy rules.

dependencies.purpose: Create two member accounts as User A and User B.
Generate a notification for User A.

scenarios.draft: Ensure that when attempting to retrieve a soft-deleted notification (deleted_at set), the system returns a not found or forbidden error, and the information is not exposed in the response.

dependencies.purpose: Create a test member to own the notification.
Create a notification for testing deletion.
Soft-delete the notification before attempting retrieval.

scenarios.draft: Verify that an administrator can create a manual/system notification event for a user with all required fields. Register an admin and a recipient member. Admin triggers a notification specifying category, preview text, recipient, and optional trigger_actor_id. Validate that the notification is correctly delivered and retrievable for the target member.

dependencies.purpose: Create both administrator and member recipient accounts to fulfill RBAC and notification delivery requirements.

scenarios.draft: Check that users without administrator role (such as members or moderators) cannot create arbitrary manual/system notifications. Attempt to post a notification as a non-admin and ensure the request is rejected.

dependencies.purpose: Create member and moderator accounts for negative authorization test.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to create a notification without specifying required fields such as recipient_member_id or notification type. Validate that the system returns appropriate validation errors and prevents creation of the notification.

dependencies.purpose: Create an administrator account to act as the sender.

scenarios.draft: Ensure that a notification recipient can successfully update a notification to mark it as read. Create a notification for a user, then update its status as the same user and confirm the read field changes and audit fields update accordingly.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member account to use as recipient.
Create a notification for the member.

scenarios.draft: Test that administrators and moderators may update notifications (such as for moderation, preview updates) for other users, but only allowed mutable fields change. Attempt various updates as privileged roles and check for correct permissions and field restrictions.

dependencies.purpose: Create member, moderator, and administrator accounts to set up permissions.
Seed test notifications for recipient member.

scenarios.draft: Verify that attempts to update a soft-deleted notification result in an error and do not change the object's state. Create and delete a notification, then attempt to update its read status or preview text.

dependencies.purpose: Prepare a test member account.
Create a notification to be deleted.
Perform the soft-delete action before update.

scenarios.draft: Verify that a user (member, moderator, or administrator) can delete a notification addressed to them only, and that the deleted_at field is set, preventing future listing or retrieval. Create a notification for a member and delete it as the same user.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member to target for deletion scenario.
Create a notification for the deletion scenario.

scenarios.draft: Test that it is impossible for a user to delete a notification that is not addressed to them unless they are an admin or moderator with the correct privilege. Create a notification for User A; attempt to delete as User B and expect forbidden error. Verify that only privileged roles (admin/mod) can delete notifications for others.

dependencies.purpose: Create accounts for User A (notification recipient) and User B (unauthorized actor), plus an admin/mod for positive path.
Generate a notification addressed to User A.

scenarios.draft: Check that deleting a notification that is already deleted or non-existent yields a not-found error or appropriate indication. Create a notification, delete it, then attempt to delete again and confirm the error handling is correct.

dependencies.purpose: Register a test member.
Seed with a test notification.
First soft-delete the notification for idempotence test.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a paginated and filtered list of categories using the PATCH /discussionBoard/categories endpoint. Verify that categories can be searched by keyword, filtered by creation/update dates, sorted, and paginated according to provided parameters. Ensure the results return expected summaries, total counts, navigation metadata, and only include undeleted categories unless filters specify otherwise. Confirm that the endpoint supports both public (guest/member) and admin usage, returning proper data according to permissions.

dependencies.purpose: Create multiple categories with distinct names and descriptions for filtering and pagination test cases. This step is required to ensure sufficient data exists for search and paging scenarios.

scenarios.draft: Test the PATCH /discussionBoard/categories endpoint with an unlikely keyword or invalid filter criteria to ensure the system returns an empty array/page and appropriate pagination metadata. This validates robustness and proper handling of queries that match no categories.

Test retrieving a specific discussion_board_category by its UUID using the GET /discussionBoard/categories/{id} endpoint. First, create a category using the POST endpoint, then fetch its details by ID and confirm that all metadata (name, description, timestamps, status) are accurately returned. Validate that the correct record is retrieved and all expected fields are present.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new category and retrieve its UUID for later detail retrieval. Necessary context for verifying detail view operation.

scenarios.draft: Test the behavior of GET /discussionBoard/categories/{id} with a non-existent or already-deleted UUID. Confirm that the response is a 404 not found error and does not leak any sensitive information. Ensures robust handling of invalid or deleted resource access attempts.

Test successful category creation by POST /discussionBoard/categories with a unique name and valid description. Confirm that the returned object matches the sent data and includes system-generated metadata (UUID, timestamps).

Test that creating a category with a name that already exists results in an error (duplicate constraint violation). First create a category, then attempt to create another with the same name. Expect a conflict or validation error response, confirming the uniqueness enforcement on name.

dependencies.purpose: Create the first category with a specific name to establish a duplication scenario for the follow-up request.

scenarios.draft: Test creating a category while omitting required fields such as 'name'. The system should reject the request with validation error, ensuring field requirements are enforced.

Test updating an existing discussion board category via PUT /discussionBoard/categories/{id} by changing its name and description. First, create a category, then update it with valid new values and verify the record reflects those changes and timestamps are updated. Validate name uniqueness as part of update process.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new category to supply a valid ID for the update scenario.

scenarios.draft: Test updating a category's name to a value that matches another existing category's name. Create two categories, then attempt to update the second one to use the first's name. Expect a conflict or validation error, confirming the name uniqueness policy is enforced on update.

dependencies.purpose: Create the first category with a distinct name to use as the target of the conflict.
Create the second category which will be updated to cause the name conflict.

scenarios.draft: Test updating a category by sending a PUT to /discussionBoard/categories/{id} with a non-existent or already-deleted ID. Expect a 404 not found error response, validating that updates are only allowed to existing, active categories.

Test soft-deleting a discussion board category using DELETE /discussionBoard/categories/{id}. First, create a category, then delete it, and finally attempt to list or get the category to confirm its deleted_at is set and is excluded from normal listings by default.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new category to provide a valid target for deletion.

scenarios.draft: Test the DELETE /discussionBoard/categories/{id} endpoint with an ID that does not correspond to any category or points to an already soft-deleted category. Confirm the system returns an appropriate error (not found or conflict), ensuring robust and correct handling of invalid delete attempts.

Test the scenario for searching and listing tags by keyword using the patch endpoint. The test should provide a filter (such as a partial tag name) and pagination parameters, validate that the resulting tag list contains only tags matching the search condition, and that the paging information matches the total count. This simulates a user browsing tags in a search interface.

dependencies.purpose: Create a set of tags prior to searching, to ensure there are enough tags to hit pagination and keyword filter conditions.

scenarios.draft: Test searching for tags with a keyword that does not exist. The test should confirm that the patch endpoint returns an empty result set and valid pagination information, simulating a user searching for a non-existent tag.

dependencies.purpose: Ensure a known baseline set of tags are created beforehand, none of which include the negative test keyword.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a paginated list of all tags with no filters applied. Should confirm the system properly returns the first page of available tags, with correct paging metadata. Ensures correct operation and privacy compliance when searching without any filter.

dependencies.purpose: Create more tags than the default pagination page size (e.g. 20 if page size is 10) to verify paging behavior.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving the full details of a tag by its valid ID. The test must create a tag first, then use its ID in the GET endpoint and verify that all metadata (name, description, timestamps) is correct and matches the creation.

dependencies.purpose: Create a tag to get a valid ID for detail retrieval.

scenarios.draft: Test attempting to retrieve details for a tag that does not exist. The test should use a randomly generated UUID not associated with any tag, and confirm that the system returns an appropriate not found error, ensuring that users cannot access deleted or non-existent tags.
Test creating a new tag with a unique name and valid description. The scenario should verify that the tag is successfully persisted and returned with correct metadata fields.

Test creating a tag with a name that already exists. First create an initial tag, then attempt to create another tag with the same name. The second attempt should fail and return a conflict or validation error, enforcing uniqueness of tag names.

dependencies.purpose: Create the first tag with a given name to set up duplication scenario.

scenarios.draft: Test attempting to create a tag with invalid data, such as a missing required name or a name that violates length/content rules. This ensures that validation errors are properly handled and the tag is not created.

Test updating a tag's details (such as name or description) with valid, unique data. The test creates an initial tag, then updates it with new attributes, verifying that the update is successful and changes are reflected.

dependencies.purpose: Create the tag to be updated.

scenarios.draft: Test updating a tag so that its name conflicts with an existing tag. First, create two tags; then attempt to update the second tag to have the same name as the first, which should fail with a conflict error due to the name uniqueness rule.

dependencies.purpose: Create the first tag with the intended duplicate name.
Create a second tag to be the update target.

scenarios.draft: Test updating a tag with invalid input, such as an empty name or incorrect format. The update operation should return a validation error and leave the tag unchanged.

dependencies.purpose: Create the tag to be updated.

scenarios.draft: Test soft-deleting a tag by its ID. The test creates a tag, deletes it using the delete endpoint, and then attempts to access it via get to ensure it is no longer returned in normal queries, confirming soft-delete works as expected and the tag is invisible for normal use.

dependencies.purpose: Create a tag to be deleted.

scenarios.draft: Test attempting to delete a tag that does not exist. Use an arbitrary UUID not associated with any tag, and ensure the endpoint returns a not found error and does not affect the system state.

Test attempting to delete a tag that was already deleted (soft-deleted). The scenario should create and delete a tag, then attempt to delete the same tag again and expect a conflict or not-modified response, ensuring idempotency and correctness of soft-delete logic.

dependencies.purpose: Create a tag to be deleted.
Delete the tag the first time to set up the repeat-delete error scenario.

scenarios.draft: Test listing threads with different search and filter conditions including keyword, creator, pinned status, category, and closed status. An authenticated user and a moderator should be able to use advanced filters and pagination controls. Ensure results match filters, and pagination metadata is correct. Verify that role-based result access restricts visibility according to permissions (e.g., guest cannot see deleted threads). Include failure scenarios such as invalid parameters or unauthorized access.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member to test authenticated and unauthenticated access to thread listing.
Create a category to be used as a filter parameter for thread listing.
Create several threads with different attributes (creator, status, category, pinned) to verify search/filter results cover all conditions.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving full thread details for an existing thread by ID as a guest, member, moderator, and admin. Validate access permissions: make sure users can only see threads per their access policies, e.g., deleted or closed threads may be hidden for some roles. Also, attempt to fetch a non-existent or deleted thread to verify proper error responses (404/not found, forbidden, etc.).

dependencies.purpose: Register a member account for testing member and owner retrieval scenarios.
Create a category to categorize the thread.
Create a thread to be retrieved by ID.

scenarios.draft: Test thread creation with valid required data (title, body, category reference) as a member. Ensure successful creation and returned thread object is correct. Attempt to create a thread with missing required fields, invalid title/body length, invalid category, or as an unauthorized user (guest or banned account). Validate that proper error messages and permission errors are returned. Verify that the creator is correctly associated and thread is open by default.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member account to be used as the authenticated user in thread creation tests.
Create a valid category to be set as thread category for creation.

scenarios.draft: Test updating thread fields (title, body, pinned/closed status) as the thread owner, as a moderator/admin, and as an unauthorized member. Ensure thread owner can update their thread with valid data, that moderator/admin can moderate/pin/close, and that a non-owner without privilege is denied. Attempt updates with invalid data (excessive length, forbidden changes) and update to a deleted thread. Confirm error responses are provided for permission violations and invalid fields.

dependencies.purpose: Register two member accounts: one as the thread owner and one as another unrelated member to test ownership and authorization.
Create a category for the thread.
Create a thread with the owner member for update scenarios.

scenarios.draft: Test soft-deleting a thread by the thread owner, by a moderator/admin, and by a non-owner member. Ensure that only the author and users with the correct role can delete, and the operation leaves thread in a soft-deleted state (deleted_at populated). Attempt to delete an already-deleted thread and a non-existent thread to verify correct error handling. After deletion, verify that audit log entries exist and that the thread is not returned in standard thread lists, except to authorized roles.

dependencies.purpose: Register three accounts: one for the thread owner, one with moderator/admin rights, and one ordinary member for permission checks.
Create a category for the target thread.
Create the thread intended for deletion.

scenarios.draft: Test listing moderator assignments with various filters and pagination. Verify administrators can retrieve paginated/moderated lists, filter by assignment status (active/revoked), time window, and search by member attributes (username/display name). Ensure empty results are returned properly if filters match no moderator. Validate permission enforcement for non-admin users attempting access (should be denied).

dependencies.purpose: Create test members to assign as moderators for search and filter purposes.
Assign moderator role to a member to ensure at least one moderator is in result set before filtering.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieval of moderator assignment details by ID. Cover both successful retrieval (admin or moderator requesting valid assignment ID) and error cases for non-existent or deleted moderator IDs, as well as unauthorized access by non-privileged users. Ensure audit-trail fields (assignment/revoked dates, linked member info, status) are present and correct.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member to assign as a moderator.
Assign moderator role to the created member so there is a valid moderator assignment to retrieve.

scenarios.draft: Test assigning moderator privileges to an existing member. Validate that admin can assign moderator to a member and receive full assignment info. Next, attempt to assign the same member again, expecting an error for duplicate assignment. Ensure that assignment links moderator to the correct member and timestamps are correct. Also check for conflict if trying to assign a member who is already an administrator.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member eligible to receive moderator assignment.

scenarios.draft: Test failure flow when attempting to assign moderator role to a non-existent member ID. Ensure the operation returns a relevant error for invalid or non-existent members and is not successful.

Test updating an existing moderator assignment by ID as administrator. Scenarios include revoking moderator privileges (setting revoked_at), updating mutable fields such as notes/context, and handling error conditions for already-revoked or non-existent moderators. Verify all changes update audit fields and assignment status appropriately.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member to assign as moderator.
Assign moderator role to the member before attempting to update.

scenarios.draft: Test revoking and soft-deleting moderator assignment by ID as administrator. Cover both successful revocation and key error flows: trying to delete a non-existent assignment, attempting double-deletion, and verifying proper audit log/audit field updates. Verify that member remains active but loses moderator privileges after revocation. Permissions must restrict operation to administrators only.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member to assign as moderator.
Assign moderator role to the member for a valid deletion scenario.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a paginated, filtered list of member accounts by supplying different combinations of search parameters (username, display name, email, activation state, date range, etc.). Confirm the endpoint correctly returns members matching each filter, paginates results as requested, and exposes only the proper fields per privacy requirements. Also validate that non-privileged users cannot access this endpoint, and that invalid filter or pagination parameters (e.g., out-of-range page size, syntactically invalid email) return appropriate error responses. Edge cases: empty result set, page out of range, and filters that yield partial matches only. Business rule: Only staff (administrator, moderator) can list members.

dependencies.purpose: Creates at least one member account so the list endpoint has data to return and filter. Multiple members with varied attributes should be created to properly test filter scenarios.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a member's detailed account profile using their UUID as an administrator or moderator. Validate that the complete set of atomic properties is returned for an existing member, and privacy rules exclude sensitive data according to the requestor's role. Test using a valid member ID and verify all expected fields. Failure case: supply a non-existent or already-deleted member UUID and check that a 404 or appropriate error is returned. Edge case: attempt to access another member's details as a non-staff user and confirm proper permission denial. Ensure audit trail and privacy compliance through output verification.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new member so a valid UUID is available for the detail retrieval test.

scenarios.draft: Test registering a new member account by providing all required information, such as username, email, password, display name, and activation state. Verify that a member is properly registered, receive the created entity, and that optional fields like profile image are handled if included. Failure scenarios: attempt to register using duplicate email or username, a password that does not meet complexity requirements, or invalid emails. The responses must clearly indicate the violation (uniqueness, validation, etc.), and successful cases must exclude sensitive fields from the output according to role. Edge case: registration with missing required fields.

Test updating a member's profile by both an administrator/moderator (with full edit rights) and as the member themselves (self-profile update). Validate that only allowed fields may be changed according to role, all audit trails are updated, and changes are properly reflected in subsequent retrievals. Also test business rules such as username/email uniqueness, password policy enforcement, and allowed changes to activation state or roles. Failure scenarios: attempt update with invalid data, duplicate email, insufficient permissions (third-party user update), or non-existent member ID, and confirm error handling matches requirements.

dependencies.purpose: Registers a new member account for update testing.

scenarios.draft: Test soft-deleting a member by their UUID as an administrator. Confirm that the member's deleted_at timestamp is set, account is deactivated, and member is marked as deleted in all future listings and detail retrievals. Ensure deletion is not allowed for members who are already deleted and for non-existent accounts, and confirm that the system returns the appropriate error. Validate that all related audit/trace fields are updated, and deactivated users cannot log in or perform actions post-delete. Edge case: member is involved in ongoing moderation role—verify related records are also soft-deleted as per the specification.

dependencies.purpose: Registers a member to be deleted in the test.

scenarios.draft: As a system administrator, fetch a paginated and filtered list of administrator assignments to review all active and historical admin roles. Include scenarios where filters are applied (e.g., by active status, assignment or member name), and where no results are returned. Validate that only authenticated administrators can access this endpoint, and unauthorized roles (such as moderators or members) receive appropriate permission errors. Verify that pagination boundaries (first/last page) are handled and that sensitive member linkage is visible according to RBAC. Edge case: Test input validation errors for malformed filter data or pagination parameters.

Confirm data includes member linkage and all assignment/revocation details.

Attempt to assign administrator role to a non-existent member and ensure suitable error (404 not found). Test RBAC enforcement by performing the operation as a non-admin user and confirming access is denied.

dependencies.purpose: Register member accounts intended for administrator assignment tests; at least two are needed for valid and duplicate role assignments.

Attempt to delete an already-deleted or non-existent assignment and verify error (404 not found or double-delete prevention). Confirm only administrators may perform deletion and that all access is logged.

dependencies.purpose: Create one or more search history records with different users as actors, capturing search keywords, date/time, and filters, so you can attempt to retrieve them by ID.

dependencies.purpose: Establish a member for warning assignment.

dependencies.purpose: Member setup: create a user to assign a warning to.

event.review:
Strengths:
- The test covers both the happy path (successful creation) and negative/error scenarios (duplicate, missing required fields).
- Random values for code and name ensure uniqueness between test runs and avoid unintended flakiness.

event.scenario:
Test soft-deleting a moderation report both as the report owner and as a moderator.

Step-by-step plan:

1. Register a general user account (Member A).
2. Register a moderator account (Member B) and grant moderator role.
3. Member A creates a post (using a new thread UUID for test isolation).
4. Member A files a moderation report against the post.
5. Member A deletes (soft deletes) their own report. Verify: report is soft-deleted (deleted_at set), is hidden from regular listings (cannot be retrieved by standard means), but is present for audit retrieval (by a moderator account).
6. Attempt to delete the same report again (double-deletion) — expect conflict or no-op error.
7. Attempt to delete a random non-existent report ID — expect not-found error.
8. Moderator (Member B) files another report; moderator deletes that report. Validate report is soft-deleted and visible via audit trail.
9. Attempt to delete a report as an unrelated, unauthorized user — expect forbidden error and that the report is not touched.
10. Audit log/data retention is validated by ensuring soft-deleted reports are still present for compliance if retrieved by elevated permissions (moderator).

Note: Since there are no explicit report listing or report fetch endpoints in the provided API, verification will be limited to type coherence and that delete operations succeed or error as expected (e.g., forbidden, not-found, or conflict), checked with type assertion and error validation. Actual audit trail verification involving listing or retrieval by elevated roles is constrained by the available functions and will be omitted in code (mention in doc and comments where not technically feasible).

Business rules and edge cases:
- Only report owners or assigned moderators can soft-delete a report.
- Non-owners and non-moderators attempting deletion should be rejected (unauthorized/forbidden).
- Soft-deleted reports retain their record (for audit/recovery purposes) but are not in default listings.
- Deleting an already-deleted or non-existent report triggers error (conflict or not-found).

## 코드 리뷰 및 품질 평가 (Korean)

### 타입 및 문법
- 함수와 변수 모두 올바른 타입으로 선언되었으며, type bypass (`any`, `as any`, `@ts-ignore` 등) 없이 구현됨
- 모든 API 응답은 `typia.assert()`로 타입 검증 후 사용
- 파라미터 타입, 함수 시그니처 구조 문제 없음

### Test Workflow 및 시나리오 적용
- 단계별로 멤버 생성, 포스트 작성, 신고 접수, 모더레이터 생성 및 지정, 신고 수정, 권한 및 상태 검증 등 실제 운영 흐름 전체 구현
- 정상 플로우(모더레이터 승인/노트작성), 권한 없음(member), 유효하지 않은 status 입력 등 오류 케이스 분리
- 변수가 적절하게 명명되어 가독성 및 의미 전달에 용이함
- 각 단계별 business 목적과 validation이 comment와 assertion으로 설명됨

### 랜덤 데이터 생성 및 의존성 처리
- 이메일, username, thread id 등은 typia/RandomGenerator로 유효하게 생성
- test isolation을 위해 모든 테스트 데이터는 독립적으로 생성됨

### assertion/검증
- 모든 주요 상태(승인, 노트, 모더레이터 id 등)와 resolved_at(live timestamp) 체크
- 권한 없음, invalid status는 TestValidator.error로 예외 기대 체크

### 타입 안전성과 품질
- 실제 DTO와 API 시그니처만 사용, 시나리오 요구를 충실히 따름
